source_snapshot.items: Test BMC I2C-6 connectivity to Mezzanine Network Board2 IO expander and FRU
source_snapshot.procedure: On BMC bus5, run the literal `i2c detect -y -q 5`, read mux0x76, write0x02 for port1, then repeat detection; consult PID1114953.
source_snapshot.criteria: Only generic result/photo collection and unexpected-log checks; no address or register-level oracle is defined.
source_snapshot.deepseek: NO; invents probing/soldering/photos as the test instead of evaluating the provided remote bus-delta method.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: MANUAL ONLY/CHANGED; notices command-name ambiguity and write risk but still incorrectly makes physical probing decisive.
source_snapshot.items_direct_xlsx: Test connections between BMC I2C-6 and Mezzanine Network Board 2 IO expander and FRU
source_snapshot.procedure_direct_xlsx: 【Before Test】 1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition. 2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.). Log into the BMC and run the following command and ensure you get a reply. Refer to PID : 1114953 for other devices expected on the bus. i2c detect -y -q 5 i2cget -f -y 5 0x76 #Read MUX ports enabled i2ctransfer -y 5 w1@0x76 0x02 #Enable MUX Port1 i2c detect -y -q 5
source_snapshot.criteria_direct_xlsx: 【After Test】 1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders. 2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.

test_case.test_name: Test connections between BMC I2C-6 and Mezzanine Network Board 2 IO expander and FRU — retained controlled review-layer procedure
test_case.purpose: Demonstrate that selecting mux0x76 port1 exposes the expected Mezzanine Network Board2 IO expander and FRU on BMC I2C-6, with device-specific replies and no unintended bus impact.
required_package: Expected Board2 IO-expander address, safe identity/status register and value/mask
Expected FRU EEPROM address, safe read offset/length and immutable signature/checksum oracle
Installed i2c-tools command set and owner-approved replacement for literal `i2c detect -y -q 5`
Mux0x76 byte semantics, bus owner/exclusive window and original-state restoration
Timeout/NACK/error criteria plus independent BMC recovery
test_case.test_command: Map BMC I2C-6 to bus5 and PID1114953 Board2 topology; inventory expected upstream and port1 addresses; capture mux state/ownership; select0x02 only with approval; perform safe address-specific IO-expander identity/status and FRU signature/header reads; compare pre/post visibility; restore the exact mux byte and verify bus/BMC health.
test_case.expected_result: 【After Test】 1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders. 2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.

Confirm physical probing is not mandatory unless separately scoped.
safety_gate: Do not run an unresolved `i2c detect` spelling or broad quick-write scan
Do not probe arbitrary addresses; use only PID-approved non-mutating endpoint reads
Confirm no daemon/driver owns bus5 or mux0x76 before forced/raw access
Capture original mux byte and preserve any required channel bits rather than assuming0x02 replacement is harmless
Abort on unexpected address delta, NACK, arbitration loss, stuck bus, FRU/IO-expander anomaly or BMC degradation; restore exact state
expected_evidence: PID1114953 excerpt mapping bus5/mux0x76/port1 to Network Board2 IO expander and FRU
Board2 identity, BMC identity/tools version, bus owner and management-health baseline
Original mux byte and approved0x02 selection/readback interpretation
Pre/post exact endpoint matrix: address, safe register/offset, expected and observed IO-expander/FRU values/checksums, exit status and timestamp
Evidence no unrelated bus5 addresses/channels or BMC services regressed
Exact mux restoration/readback, endpoint health and engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: Under Wistron I2C policy this is BMC/platform-management scope. Controller, bus, mux, endpoint addresses, safe request semantics, expected replies and OOB recovery are mandatory.

source_conflict.reason: The literal `i2c detect` command is not established as a valid installed tool, `-q` discovery is not accompanied by an approved per-device safety contract, Criteria lacks expected Board2 addresses/content, and earlier reviews invent mandatory probing/soldering.
